user.title: Select your vehicle and price entities
user.description: BitCruise reads entities that already exist in Home Assistant. Nothing here is vendor specific.

data_description.soc_entity: The vehicle's current state of charge, in percent.
data_description.target_entity:
Optional. How full the car should be charged, in percent. Leave empty to set a fixed target on the next page.

Make sure this is a percentage. Cars often also expose a 'charging limit' measured in amps, which controls how fast it charges, not how full it gets. A target of 16 or 32 is a sign you have picked that one by mistake.
data_description.capacity_entity: Optional. Usable battery capacity in kWh or Wh. Leave empty to enter it on the next page.
data_description.plug_entity: Optional. Either a binary sensor, or a sensor reporting connected or disconnected.
data_description.availability_entity: Optional, but recommended. Reports whether the vehicle is reachable. Used to detect readings that may be out of date, so charging is never planned from a stale battery level.
data_description.price_entity: Optional for now. Used from the next release onward to find the cheapest charging window.

settings.title: Charging settings
settings.description: Values used to work out how much energy is needed and how long it will take.

data_description.target_fixed_pct: Used only when no charge target entity was selected.
data_description.capacity_fixed_kwh: Used only when no capacity entity was selected.
data_description.charging_power_kw: Roughly 11 kW for a 16 A three-phase supply, or 7.4 kW for 32 A single phase.
data_description.charging_efficiency: Energy reaching the battery as a share of energy drawn from the grid. Around 90 percent is typical.
data_description.reserve_floor_pct:
NOT ACTIVE YET — leave this at 0 unless you are experimenting. Acting on it arrives in a later release; for now it is only recorded.

What it will do: the charge target asks 'how full by the deadline?', while the reserve floor asks 'could I just get in and drive, right now?'. Charging at the cheapest hours deliberately leaves the battery low until shortly before your deadline, which is unhelpful if someone needs the car unexpectedly. The floor is the level you never want to sit below — drop under it and BitCruise will charge straight away instead of waiting for cheap power.

It must be lower than the charge target, because it is a minimum rather than a second target. Something like 30 to 40 percent is typical.
data_description.ready_by: The time the vehicle should be charged by.
data_description.not_before: Optional. Prevents charging being scheduled earlier than this time.

error.target_required: Select a charge target entity, or set a fixed target.
error.capacity_required: Select a battery capacity entity, or enter the capacity.
error.floor_above_target: The reserve floor must be lower than the charge target. It is the level you never want to drop below, not a second target. Set it to 0 if you do not want to use it.
error.target_not_a_percentage: That entity is not measured in percent. A 'charging limit' in amps controls how fast the car charges, not how full it gets. Pick the entity that reports the charge target as a percentage, or leave this empty and set a fixed target on the next page.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single BitCruise instance is supported.
